sources.title: Nizet Lab
sources.text: Nizet Lab Team The Nizet Lab has more than two dozen students, postdocs, staff, visiting scholars, and affiliated faculty. Meet the Team Nizet Lab Recently, a new graduate student and two postdocs have joined the lab. More News Research The Nizet lab investigates innate immunity, bacterial pathogenesis, therapeutics and vaccines against sepsis and multidrug resistant pathogens. Research Our Publications The Nizet lab published hundreds of papers, contributing our understanding of host pathogen interactions, bacterial pathogenesis, and the development and repurposing of therapeutics effective against multidrug resistant pathogens. More Publications Previous Next About Research Team News Publications Collaborators Calendar Contact About Us The interest of the Nizet laboratory lies in understanding fundamental mechanisms of bacterial pathogenesis and the innate immune system, with a special focus on human streptococcal, staphylococcal and multidrug resistant Gram-negative bacterial infections. Using a combination of molecular genetics, microbiology, proteomics, immunology, and murine models of infection, we seek to identify and develop novel biotherapeutics, antimicrobials, and vaccines to further translational medicine in the fight against MDR infections. Learn More Research Focus Bacterial Pathogenesis Innate Immune System Therapeutics & Vaccines Recent News Congratulations to UCSD Pharmacy PharmD/PhD student Daniel Sun on his successful advancement to candidacy in the UCSD BMS graduate program! Great presentation to his full thesis committee on his innovative studies on alternative therapies for MRSA infections and sepsis. sources.text: Faculty Labs The Department of Pediatrics at UC San Diego is one of the nation's premier Departments devoted to improving the understanding of disease pathogenesis in order to better diagnose, treat and prevent diseases in infants and children. Research efforts include basic and clinical science in various fields spanning the whole range of maladies. Another important goal in the Department is to build and foster the development of the next generation of research leaders in Pediatric Medicine. There has been no better time for research and training in Pediatrics than what is currently and what we predict it will be in the next decade!
